description:
Price levels per ticket type, time-based/tiered pricing, and the rule hierarchy venue → series → event → price level with explicit overrides. Includes a spike: DSL vs declarative config for complex event programming (owner is open to a DSL).

**Conditions of Success:**
- A price resolves deterministically through the hierarchy with visible provenance (which level won)
- Scheduled price changes (early-bird tiers) apply without manual intervention
- DSL-vs-config spike concluded with an ADR

Lineage: docs/product/brief.md · docs/product/prd-v1.md (capability map).

comments.body: COS defined at epic level. Not yet decomposed — US-stories are created when the owner prioritizes this epic (Gate 1), per PRD 'Capability map'.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Decomposition — TKT-5 → 1 spike + 3 stories

Lineage: `docs/product/brief.md` → `docs/product/prd-v1.md` (capability map, row TKT-5).
Board backend: **local** (`.sdlc/`, state on `sdlc-state`). Decomposed by the orchestrator
(main-agent) on 2026-07-30.

| Child | Type | Slice | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| TKT-150 | Spike | Rules representation: custom DSL vs declarative config → **ADR** | — |
| TKT-151 | Story | Hierarchy resolves deterministically, with visible provenance | TKT-150 |
| TKT-152 | Story | Early-bird tiers flip by the clock alone (evaluation-time windows) | TKT-151 |
| TKT-153 | Story | The sale charges the resolved price; the reservation records why | TKT-151 |

**Mapping to the epic's COS** — every COS is owned by exactly one child, and no COS is
orphaned:

| Epic COS | Owned by |
|---|---|
| A price resolves deterministically through the hierarchy with visible provenance | TKT-151 (resolution + provenance), made durable on the sale by TKT-153 |
| Scheduled price changes (early-bird tiers) apply without manual intervention | TKT-152 |
| DSL-vs-config spike concluded with an ADR | TKT-150 |

**Why this cut.** The spike goes first because it decides the *data shape* the other three
implement — deciding it after the schema exists means a migration, not an edit. Then one story per
COS, each a vertical slice (schema → store → resolver → API → tests) that is demoable on its own:
TKT-151 by posting rules at two levels and reading back which won, TKT-152 by resolving the same
row set at two instants, TKT-153 by reserving and seeing the resolved amount and its provenance on
the reservation. Nothing here is a horizontal layer ticket.

**Service split is not ours to choose** — ADR-002 and `docs/architecture.md` already assign
*rule definitions* to `catalog` and *pricing evaluation* to `commerce`. TKT-151/152 live in
catalog; TKT-153 is the commerce side. The spike must say which side runs the evaluator, since a
DSL would put pressure on that line.

**Deliberately out of scope** (they belong to their own epics, and pulling them in here is how
this epic becomes unreviewable): service fees & revenue splits (TKT-6), promos/discount codes,
per-channel price rules and windows (TKT-17), VAT (TKT-32), combo/bundle pricing (TKT-8),
repricing on exchange/refund (TKT-9), and any back-office authoring UI for rules.

**Cycle check:** edges are 150→151, 151→152, 151→153. Walked transitively from each child; no
path returns to its start. No cycles.

**Context-mémo:** baked on all four children (local backend → the `context` object on the ticket,
per `local-tracker.md`'s substrate table). `governingAdrs` resolved from `docs/adr/` by area on
2026-07-30 — every cited ADR file was verified to exist at HEAD. The one that matters most and
that a code-reading drafter cannot discover: **ADR-030** (catalog is *out* of the smoke
happy-path coverage gate and covers its operations in its own unit coverage test, while commerce
is *in* it) — so TKT-151/152 and TKT-153 owe their coverage evidence in **different suites**.
Second: **ADR-020** (plain `CREATE INDEX`; `CONCURRENTLY` still not adopted) — the obvious
"improvement" a drafter would reach for on a new index is the wrong one here.

### ✅ Implementation readiness — CONCERNS

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Quality gates extracted | ✅ | `make check` + ADR-009 contract tests + ADR-004 TTL declaration + ADR-002 tenancy, appended to every child |
| Sizing (one reviewable PR each) | ✅ | Each child is one vertical slice; TKT-153 is the largest and is still one handler + one migration + tests |
| Prefactoring split out first | ✅ | The spike is the prefactor — it makes the change easy before the change is made |
| Ordered by dependency | ✅ | 150 → 151 → {152, 153}; no forward dependency |
| AC verifiable | ✅ | Each AC names an observable: a test that must exist, a file that must be regenerated, a value that must not move |
| Links + cycle check | ✅ | `blocked-by` edges wired; cycle check walked, clean |
| Context-mémo per child | ✅ | 4/4, `governingAdrs` included, all cited ADR files exist at HEAD |
| No unvalidated silent assumption | ⚠️ | See concerns 1 and 2 |

**Concerns:**
1. **TKT-151/152/153 cite a decision that does not exist yet.** Their ACs are written against
   "the shape TKT-150 decided". This is the correct dependency, not a defect — but per
   `decomposition.md` § *spike-amended scope*, each child's ACs **must be re-synced to the spike's
   actual decision before it reaches Ready**. Leaving a pre-spike AC that contradicts the spike
   costs a Planning cycle. This run will do that re-sync explicitly and record it.
2. **TKT-153 is a money path.** Anticipated by the epic and by this decomposition, so it is not a
   surprise — but it is the one child where a silent regression is expensive. Its ACs make the
   regression proof mechanical: *with no rules defined, behaviour is byte-identical to today and
   the existing commerce + smoke tests stay green unmodified*.
3. **TKT-152 and TKT-153 could parallelize** (both depend only on TKT-151), but this run executes
   them sequentially — WIP is one ticket, and a TDD loop does not parallelize. Noted so the
   sequence is not mistaken for a hard dependency.

**Verdict: CONCERNS** — proceedable. The decomposition is sound and every epic COS has exactly one
owner; the two named risks (spike-dependent ACs, money path) are managed by explicit steps rather
than by hope.
